audit.species: Human (Homo sapiens). Discovery arm: treatment-naive NSCLC patients (LUAD and LUSC), University Hospital Basel / Kantonsspital Baselland. Supporting in vitro arm: healthy-donor peripheral blood NK cells. No animal work in this paper.
audit.what_was_measured: In humans (11 treatment-naive NSCLC patients; 7 LUAD, 4 LUSC), at a SINGLE cross-sectional timepoint (surgical resection; no repeat sampling of any patient), FACS-sorted live CD45+CD19-CD14-CD56+ cells from cryopreserved tumour digests were lysed to nuclei and profiled by paired 10x Multiome snRNA-seq + snATAC-seq; after QC and WNN integration 29,890 high-quality NK nuclei were retained (T/B/myeloid/Treg removed computationally; T cells removed by a UCell CD3D/CD3G score < 0.05 threshold). The readout that generates the claimed transition is a COMPUTATIONAL ORDERING of the NK3 subcompartment pooled across all 11 donors: (i) MultiVelo v0.1.5 RNA+ATAC velocity streamlines on top-1000 variable genes; (ii) destiny v3.4.0 diffusion-map pseudotime, run separately on RNA and on ATAC gene-activity scores, with "the main root selected from the NK3_GZMK cluster"; (iii) Monocle3 v1.3.1 pseudotime (v1 methods) with learn_graph ncenter=100 and "the starting point defined as the terminal branch within the NK3_GZMK population"; (iv) top-100 Moran's I pseudotime-correlated genes (CD44/GZMK early -> IFIT3/IFI44/ISG15/GZMB mid -> KLRC1/LAYN/ENTPD1/ITGAE/KLRC2/GZMA late) and SCENIC+ eRegulon activity (TCF7/BACH2 -> STAT1/NFKB/FOS/JUNB/RUNX2) plotted along that same pseudotime. Protein-level work measured STATE, not transition: flow cytometry of CD45+CD14-CD19-CD3-CD56+ cells from an independent cohort (tumour n=15, adjacent lung n=13, blood n=12; marker panel n=14; GZMA in CD39+ vs CD39- n=11); 5/24 h restimulation with IL-12/IL-15/IL-18 or irradiated K562 (n=8; CD39+/- comparison n=7); 48 h anti-NKG2A (monalizumab biosimilar) vs isotype in patient-derived tumour fragments (n=7); 10x Xenium spatial transcriptomics on ONE LUAD patient (LuT-722). In the published version only, an in vitro platform: healthy-donor blood NK + IL-15 + TGF-beta +/- irradiated A549 (10:1) for 6 days, flow + bulk RNA-seq at day 6, then sorted CD103+CD49a+CD39+/- cells in 24 h A549-b2m-ko killing assays (n=6-7 donors). NO cell, clone, donor or nucleus was tracked over time; no GZMK+ NK cell was sorted and re-assayed; no barcoding, no mtDNA clonal tracing, no transfer, no genetic fate map.
audit.n_unit: patients (treatment-naive NSCLC donors) contributing nuclei to the multiome dataset on which the ENTIRE trajectory claim rests; the NK3 cells were POOLED across these 11 donors and no per-donor replication of the trajectory (or leave-one-donor-out) is reported. Validation cohorts, all in donors/patients: flow tumour n=15, adjacent lung n=13, blood n=12, marker panel n=14, CD39+/- GZMA n=11, restimulation n=8 (CD39 split n=7), PDTF anti-NKG2A n=7, in vitro taNK platform/killing n=6-7 healthy donors, Xenium n=1 patient. Public comparison data: 50 non-tumour lung donors (Sikkema/Bischoff). Cell counts (57,854 total; 29,890 NK nuclei) are NOT n.
audit.controls: (1) Non-tumour comparison tissue: adjacent non-tumour lung and peripheral blood by flow (n=13, n=12), plus integration with two public non-tumour lung NK datasets (Sikkema, Bischoff; 20,198 NK cells from 50 donors) — establishes that the ENTPD1+/CD103+/CD49a+ state is tumour-restricted. (2) Internal cell-intrinsic comparator: CD103-CD49a- (and CD39-) NK from the same digest, with paired non-parametric statistics. (3) Isotype IgG4 control for anti-NKG2A in PDTFs, plus target-engagement check (surface NKG2A loss). (4) Unstimulated and tumour-cell-only baselines in restimulation/killing assays. (5) QC/artefact controls: patient-specific stress cluster (Cluster 5, one patient) excluded; histone/ribosomal gene blacklist; mitochondrial % regressed; CCA/LSI donor batch correction; ATAC diffusion component 1 discarded as sequencing-quality-driven; CD3D used in Xenium to exclude T cells. MISSING CONTROLS RELEVANT TO THE LINEAGE CLAIM: no alternative-root / root-free trajectory analysis (root was analyst-placed in NK3_GZMK in both Monocle3 and destiny); no per-donor or held-out-donor reproduction of the trajectory; NK1/NK2/ILC1 compartments were EXCLUDED before trajectory inference, so no non-NK3 progenitor could have been recovered by construction; no protein-level (CITE-seq/hashing) confirmation that the transcriptomically CD3-low NK3_ENTPD1 nuclei are truly CD3-negative NK rather than NK-like/CD3-dim T cells (the cluster expresses CD3E, IL32, CTLA4, CXCL13, LAYN); no negative-control trajectory on a population known not to interconvert.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: NK3_GZMK and NK3_ENTPD1 are two independently seeded/maintained states that sit adjacent in expression space, not a precursor and its product. Concretely: (a) GZMK marks CD56bright NK — Bratke 2005 (PMID 16106370) shows ALL CD56bright NK are GZMK+ while GZMB is confined to CD56dim, and the paper itself annotates NK3_GZMK by CD56bright genes (CD44, GZMK, CXCR4) — so NK3_GZMK is plausibly recently-immigrated circulating CD56bright NK, while NK3_ENTPD1 is a locally imprinted (TGF-beta/IL-15) tissue-resident state, or a pre-existing adaptive-like CD49a+CD103+NKG2C+ lung trNK population that expands in tumour (Brownlie 2021, PMID 33836578 — these cells exist in HEALTHY human lung and blood). Under that model the "trajectory" recovers a residency/maturation gradient plus donor-to-donor mixing, not a conversion. (b) The ordering's DIRECTION is not data-derived: the Monocle3 start point was "defined as the terminal branch within the NK3_GZMK population" and the destiny root "selected from the NK3_GZMK cluster"; MultiVelo streamlines on single-NUCLEUS data (intron-dominated, spliced/unspliced ratios distorted relative to whole-cell scRNA-seq) supplied the prior for that choice. Root choice, not biology, fixes GZMK as "early". (c) The ISG-high midpoint (IFIT3, IFI44, ISG15) is more parsimoniously an acute, reversible interferon-response state layered on any NK cell than a differentiation waypoint — ISG-high clusters recur across cell types and conditions and can be induced or lost within hours. (d) ENTPD1/CD39 is an activation-inducible ectoenzyme, not a lineage mark: the authors themselves induce it on healthy-donor blood NK within 6 days with IL-15+TGF-beta, so the "endpoint" may be a reversible activation state occupied and vacated by many cells. (e) Technical: sorting was CD45+CD19-CD14-CD56+CD3+ (NK plus T) with T cells removed only by a transcriptomic CD3D/CD3G threshold; NK3_ENTPD1 carries a CD8-Trm/tumour-reactive program (CD3E, IL32, CTLA4, CXCL13, LAYN, ITGAE, ENTPD1), so residual CD3-dim T cells, T-NK doublet nuclei or ambient signal would create exactly the observed "endpoint" and exactly the observed apparent gradient from a bona fide NK cluster toward it. The Xenium CD3D check was one patient and does not address doublets in the multiome.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, including from the paper itself. (1) SELF-CONTRADICTING, same paper, published version: a new "Cross-modality analysis suggests distinct epigenetic origins" section concludes that the two taNK branches "represent distinct lineages that converge transcriptionally, while retaining their ancestral chromatin marks" (NK3_CRTAM/CAMK4 -> ATAC cluster a2; NK3_ENTPD1 -> ATAC cluster a6) — i.e. the authors endorse independent origins for the sister branch of the very bifurcation whose root is GZMK. (2) SELF-HEDGING, same paper: for the only time-resolved experiment (48 h PDTF anti-NKG2A) they write "Anti-NKG2A therapy either expands existing CD39+GZMA+ and CD39+GZMB+ populations or promotes their induction from CD39- precursors", and in the discussion "their exact origin remains unresolved... both circulating and pre-existing tissue-resident NK cells may contribute", and CRTAM+ cells "may represent a tissue-resident, adaptive-like subset that expands upon tumour progression... this interpretation remains speculative". (3) Brownlie et al., PNAS 2021, PMID 33836578 (archived): adaptive-like CD49a+CD103+NKG2C+ CD56bright trNK are already present in healthy human lung and in blood with donor-variable expansions — a pre-existing, selectable subset, i.e. the canonical alternative, and re-entry from tissue to blood is proposed. (4) Mogilenko et al., Immunity 2021, PMID 33271118 (archived): in the better-characterised CD8 compartment, GZMK+ cells (Taa) are a highly CLONAL, epigenetically distinct population separate from Tem, not an obligatory transitional precursor — cautionary counter-analogy for reading "GZMK+" as "early". (5) Tang et al., Cell 2023, PMID 37607536 (archived; 716 patients, 24 cancer types): the tumour-enriched NK population identified pan-cancer shows IMPAIRED anti-tumour function and associates with UNFAVOURABLE prognosis and immunotherapy RESISTANCE — the opposite functional valence to Serger's CD39+ "effector" endpoint, undermining the "culminates in an effector state" framing. (6) Horowitz et al., Sci Transl Med 2026, PMID 42090477 (archived): CD39+CD49a+CD103+ cytotoxic trNK can be differentiated ex vivo from PERIPHERAL NK and control mouse tumours — supports inducibility of the endpoint phenotype but from a different starting population and via TGF-beta, not via a GZMK+ intratumoural precursor or an ISG-driven route, so it does not corroborate this specific transition. (7) NEGATIVE SEARCH RESULT (searched, not found): no clonal or mitochondrial-variant lineage-tracing study of human intratumoural NK subsets was located (query "mitochondrial variant lineage tracing natural killer cells human" returned 0 PubMed hits); no independent dataset reproducing a GZMK+ -> ENTPD1+ NK ordering was found.
audit.downstream_dependency: Named, concrete: (1) The paper's own ex vivo "in vitro taNK cell platform" for adoptive cell therapy — healthy-donor blood NK + IL-15 + TGF-beta + irradiated A549 for 6 days to manufacture CD103+CD49a+CD39+ NK — is designed on the premise that the CD39+ ISG-high state is an INDUCIBLE endpoint of NK differentiation rather than a fixed pre-existing lineage; every killing/NKG2A result in Figs. 4E, 6E and 7D-F is generated in those induced cells and read back onto primary taNK biology. (2) The NKG2A-blockade rationale ("CD39+ taNK emerge upon anti-NKG2A"), explicitly tied to the monalizumab biosimilar and phase 3 trial NCT05221840 in NSCLC — if CD39+ cells are selected rather than induced, "emergence" is expansion of a fixed pool with a hard ceiling, a different therapeutic prediction. (3) Within this screen (/home/user/aaa/phaseA/claims.json): X4's directionality is inherited from claim D3 ("Human CD56bright NK -> CD56dim NK", itself graded MOSTLY INFERENCE) because GZMK marks CD56bright and GZMB/CD39 the CD56dim-like pole (Bratke 2005, PMID 16106370) — X4 cannot be stronger than D3. It is also the concrete instance backing claims X1 ("organ-resident trNK -> functional intratumoural NK") and X2 ("newly infiltrating NK -> dysfunctional tumour NK"), which assume intratumoural NK states are connected by local differentiation. Rated MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the paper's headline conclusions (CD39 marks the dominant cytotoxic taNK population; NKG2A blockade potentiates it) are cross-sectional/functional and survive intact if the transition is false.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: Claude's initial call — INFERENCE, Serger 2026 snRNA+snATAC trajectory — is CONFIRMED on every element, and the citation is real (PMID 42247486, Sci Immunol 2026;11(120):eaeb6645; preprint 10.1101/2025.08.26.672316), not misremembered. The audit sharpens rather than overturns it, in four ways. (a) Exact class: INF_TRAJECTORY, the weakest class, by rule G2 — MultiVelo velocity + destiny diffusion pseudotime + Monocle3 pseudotime + SCENIC+ regulons ordered along that pseudotime, on one cross-sectional snapshot from 11 pooled donors. (b) The direction is partly ASSUMED, not inferred: both pseudotime methods had their root manually placed inside NK3_GZMK ("the starting point was defined as the terminal branch within the NK3_GZMK population"; "the main root was selected from the NK3_GZMK cluster"), and the trajectory was run only on the NK3 subcompartment, so alternative progenitors (NK1, NK2, ILC1) were excluded by construction. This is weaker than a plain "trajectory inference" label implies. (c) The published version adds evidence Claude's call did not account for — an in vitro platform in which IL-15+TGF-beta(+A549) induces CD103/CD49a and then CD39 on healthy-donor blood NK over 6 days (INF_INVITRO). This is a real conversion demonstration for the PHENOTYPE, but it starts from peripheral blood NK rather than intratumoural GZMK+ NK3, is driven by TGF-beta rather than the ISG/inflammation program the trajectory posits, is scored as bulk population frequencies with no single-cell tracking (IL-15 drives proliferation, so outgrowth of a competent minority is not excluded), and therefore does not raise the claim above INFERENCE. (d) The published version also adds a cross-modality analysis in which the authors themselves conclude the two taNK branches "represent distinct lineages that converge transcriptionally", and they hedge the one time-resolved experiment as "either expands existing... or promotes their induction from CD39- precursors" — so the paper's own text is closer to this audit's grading than its abstract's "revealed an inflammation-driven transition" is. No downgrade below INFERENCE is warranted either: the endpoint state is genuinely tumour-restricted (absent from 50 non-tumour lung donors and from blood), which does argue for local acquisition of the phenotype by SOME NK cell, even though nothing in the paper establishes that the cell in question was GZMK+.
audit.methods_quote: MultiVelo v0.1.5, v2 Methods: "MultiVelo was used to infer velocity trajectory based on both RNA expression and ATAC... The analysis was performed on the NK3 subset pooled across all samples." Root-setting, v1 Methods (moved to supplementary in v2): "To validate the identified transcriptional trajectories and gain deeper insight into the transition from NK3_GZMK to NK3_ENTPD1, we performed pseudotime analysis of these populations using Monocle3 (v1.3.1) on all samples combined. The learn_graph function was run with the parameter 'ncenter = 100' to prevent over-branching of the trajectory. The starting point was defined as the terminal branch within the NK3_GZMK population, based on MultiVelocity and diffusion map analyses." And: "The main root was selected from the NK3_GZMK cluster, at the beginning of the directed streamline inferred by MultiVelocity. Diffusion pseudotime for all cells was then calculated using the DPT function." Sort gate, v1/v2 Methods: "Cells were gated on single cells, live (Zombie NIR-), CD45+, CD19-CD14- and CD56+CD3+." T-cell removal, Methods: "a signature score for T cells (CD3D, CD3G) was calculated using the AddModuleScore_UCell function... Cells with a signature score higher than 0.05 were removed from the dataset in order to obtain a clean NK cell dataset." Author hedge, Results (v1): "Anti-NKG2A therapy either expands existing CD39+GZMA+ and CD39+GZMB+ populations or promotes their induction from CD39- precursors."

EVIDENCE-TYPE JUSTIFICATION. INF_TRAJECTORY (strongest, and the sole basis for the arrow): MultiVelo + destiny + Monocle3 + pseudotime-ordered SCENIC+ regulons. INF_MARKER: the "early" label on NK3_GZMK rests on CD56bright-associated marker genes (CD44, GZMK, KLRF1, CXCR4), and the flow/Xenium work confirms marker co-expression only. INF_INVITRO: the published version's 6-day IL-15+TGF-beta+A549 induction of CD103/CD49a and then CD39 on healthy-donor blood NK — genuine phenotype induction, but from the wrong starting population, via the wrong driver, read as bulk frequencies. INF_KINETIC: listed only because the paper frames the 48 h PDTF anti-NKG2A result as CD39+ taNK "emerging"; the measured quantity is GZMA/GZMB positivity WITHIN CD39+ cells, not a frequency shift of the CD39+ state, and the authors explicitly decline to distinguish expansion from induction — this element carries no lineage weight and should not be counted toward the claim. NO OBS_* class is present: no direct observation, no transfer, no genetic fate map.

TERMINOLOGY DRIFT worth flagging downstream: the middle NK3 subcluster is called NK3_CRTAM in v1 and NK3_CAMK4 in the v2 Fig. 5 legend; and "taNK" in this paper denotes a cytotoxic, prognostically FAVOURABLE population, whereas "TaNK" in Tang et al. Cell 2023 denotes a dysfunctional, prognostically UNFAVOURABLE one. Same acronym, opposite valence.

VERDICT IN ONE LINE: the claim is an analyst-rooted pseudotime/velocity ordering of one cross-sectional 11-donor snapshot, partially supported by an in vitro phenotype induction from a different starting cell — INFERENCE, weakest class, exactly as the initial call had it.

adv.challenge_reason:
UPHELD as INF_TRAJECTORY after independent re-reading of the methods (lit.py methods 42247486 -> ABSTRACT_ONLY, confirming no PMCID/OA; methods re-read from the archived author manuscripts /home/user/aaa/refs/X4_PPR_v2_biorxiv.txt and X4_PPR1074288_biorxiv.txt). Every root-setting quote in the row verifies VERBATIM: Monocle3 v1.3.1, "The starting point was defined as the terminal branch within the NK3_GZMK population, based on MultiVelocity and diffusion map analyses"; destiny v3.4.0, "The main root was selected from the NK3_GZMK cluster, at the beginning of the directed streamline inferred by MultiVelocity"; MultiVelo v0.1.5 "performed on the NK3 subset pooled across all samples". n=11 treatment-naive NSCLC patients (LUAD 7 / LUSC 4), 57,854 cells, 29,890 WNN nuclei — all verify. The arrow rests on nothing but computational ordering of one cross-sectional snapshot.

I specifically hunted for an OBS_* experiment the auditor might have MISSED, prompted by a signal the auditor did not react to: five Serger co-authors (Rackwitz, Brueggemann, Pawlow, Chichelnitskiy, Falk) are from the Institute of Transplant Immunology, Hannover Medical School — a group that owns donor/recipient chimerism, i.e. a natural OBS_TRANSFER readout. Systematic scan of BOTH versions for chimeri* / genotype / souporcell / demultiplex / hashing / CITE / clonot* / TCR / "lineage tracing" / parabio* / explant / "donor-derived": ZERO hits. "barcod" resolves only to 10x cell barcodes; "TCR" only to a discussion sentence; "HLA" only to A549-b2m-ko-HLA-E target cells. No fate map, no transfer, no barcoding, no mtDNA tracing. No OBS class exists, and the auditor credited none. UPHELD, no UPGRADE available; no DOWNGRADE either, since INF_TRAJECTORY is already the weakest class under G2.

ONE METHODS DEFECT THE AUDITOR MISSED, which strengthens its own artefact alternative: the multiome sort panel is listed in full as CD45-BV711, CD8-BV421, CD8-APC, CD19-FITC, CD14-FITC, CD56-PE — it contains NO CD3 antibody — yet the stated gate is "Cells were gated on single cells, live (Zombie NIR-), CD45+, CD19-CD14- and CD56+CD3+." The gate as written is both biologically wrong-signed (CD3+ selects T/NKT) and unexecutable with the listed reagents. T-cell exclusion therefore rested entirely on the transcriptomic UCell CD3D/CD3G > 0.05 filter. Since the trajectory ENDPOINT (NK3_ENTPD1) is defined by a CD8-Trm/tumour-reactive program — CD3E, IL32, CTLA4, CXCL13, LAYN, ITGAE, ENTPD1 — residual CD3-dim T cells or T/NK doublet nuclei would manufacture exactly the observed endpoint and exactly the observed gradient running toward it from a bona fide NK cluster. The auditor flagged the gate but not the missing reagent.

Minor correction to the row: INF_KINETIC should be struck from evidence_types_all rather than merely annotated. I verified the PDTF readout is "a significant increase in the proportion of CD39+ NK cells expressing GZMB or GZMA, while the CD39- subset remained unchanged" — a granzyme shift WITHIN a fixed CD39+ gate, not a kinetic measurement of the CD39+ state's frequency. Nothing kinetic about the A->B transition was measured.
adv.revised_evidence_type_strongest: INF_TRAJECTORY (unchanged). Present, in descending weight: INF_TRAJECTORY (sole basis for the arrow — MultiVelo RNA+ATAC velocity, destiny diffusion pseudotime on RNA and on ATAC gene-activity, Monocle3 pseudotime, plus Moran's-I gene and SCENIC+ eRegulon curves plotted along that same pseudotime); INF_MARKER (the "early" label on NK3_GZMK rests on CD56bright-associated marker genes CD44/GZMK/KLRF1/CXCR4; all flow, Xenium and TCGA-deconvolution work confirms co-expression or abundance, never transition); INF_INVITRO (6-day IL-15+TGF-beta+irradiated-A549 induction of CD103/CD49a/CD39 on healthy-donor blood NK, n=6-7 donors — real phenotype induction, but from peripheral blood NK rather than intratumoural GZMK+ NK3, driven by TGF-beta rather than the ISG program the trajectory posits, and scored as bulk population frequencies under an IL-15 proliferative stimulus, so outgrowth of a competent minority is not excluded). INF_KINETIC should be REMOVED (see challenge_reason). No OBS_DIRECT, OBS_TRANSFER or OBS_GENETIC.
adv.new_counter_evidence:
FOUR items the auditor missed, the first of which is the strongest counter-evidence available and comes from the paper's OWN reference framework.

(1) REBUFFET et al., "High-dimensional single-cell analysis of human natural killer cell heterogeneity," Nat Immunol 2024, PMID 38956378 / PMC11291291 (full text read, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/X4adv_reb_PMC11291291.txt). This is the paper that DEFINES the NK1/NK2/NK3 nomenclature Serger uses; its first author Lucas Rebuffet is Serger's SECOND author and Eric Vivier is senior on both. Three findings, each destructive to X4:
 (a) GZMK is an NK2 marker there, NOT an NK3 marker. Verbatim, NK2 is defined by "CD56, CD27, CD44, CD54, CD45RB, CD314 (NKG2D)... transcription factors (TCF7)... molecules implicated in cell migration and tissue homing (CD44, GPR183, SELL), along with granzyme K (GZMK)... indicating that the NK2 population comprised CD56bright and early-stage CD56dim NK cells." NK3, by contrast, is "CD16, CD57, CD271 (NGFR), CD2, CD18, CD49d and inhibitory KIRs... PRDM1" — the most mature/adaptive pole. Serger's root cluster "NK3_GZMK" is annotated inside NK3 while carrying NK2/CD56bright markers (the paper itself says NK3_GZMK "expressed genes commonly associated with CD56bright NK cells, such as CD44 and GZMK"). A cluster bearing one subset's markers sitting at the edge of another subset is the textbook signature of two adjacent populations, not a precursor.
 (b) TWO SEPARATE ONTOGENIES, stated in the abstract: "These data also suggest two separate ontogenetic origins for NK cells, leading to divergent transcriptional trajectories," resolved in the results as "two divergent ontogenic pathways: one for NK1 and NK3, originating from ENKPs, and another for NK2, originating from ILCPs." So the root (NK2-like, ILCP-derived) and the endpoint (NK3, ENKP-derived) plausibly belong to DIFFERENT ONTOGENIES. The canonical "two independent origins" alternative is asserted by Serger's own co-authors in the paper Serger cites for its cell-type labels.
 (c) The SAME TOOLS, run by the same people on blood, gave the OPPOSITE answer: "This analysis indicated that the majority of NK2 cells would likely persist as NK2 cells, forming a specific NK2 trajectory," and diffusion-map pseudotime "highlighted a considerable gap between NK2 and NKint... reinforcing the concept of two distinct trajectories." GZMK-high cells persist as themselves. Worse, Rebuffet EXCLUDED NK3 from trajectory inference on methodological grounds: "NK3 cells, which exhibit clonal-like transcriptional dynamics owing to their interaction with HCMV, were excluded from the following trajectory analysis, to avoid having their unique transcriptional behavior skew the findings." Serger runs velocity and pseudotime on exactly the NK3 compartment the reference paper declared unsuitable for it — and Serger's endpoint expresses KLRC2/NKG2C, the adaptive-HCMV marker that motivated the exclusion.

(2) NIEHRS et al., "Transient tissue residency and lymphatic egress define human CD56bright NK cell homeostasis," Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907 (full text read; archived X4adv_egress_PMC12571907.txt). Human liver transplantation, intravascular labelling, humanized mice, non-human primates, efferent lymph sampling. Verbatim: "in human liver transplantation, donor-derived CD56bright NK cells represent the dominant TR NK cell population early after transplantation, but are replaced over time by infiltrating recipient NK cells that establish TR traits, a process partly regulated by Runx3. Transient TR CD56bright NK cells recirculated via lymphatics." Two consequences. First, tissue-residency traits are acquired by CONTINUOUSLY ARRIVING circulating cells, so a cross-sectional gradient from "recently arrived CD56bright/GZMK+" to "locally imprinted" is exactly what an influx-plus-imprinting steady state produces with zero committed differentiation. Second, and fatal to pseudotime specifically: CD56bright NK EGRESS via lymph. Pseudotime assumes cells progress one-way along a continuum; if the putative precursor pool is continuously replenished from blood AND continuously leaves, the ordering is a residency-time-and-turnover artefact, not a lineage.

(3) BELLMAS-SANZ R, ..., CHICHELNITSKIY E, ..., FALK CS. "Donor tissue-resident memory-like T and NK cells generate a transient peripheral chimerism in lung transplant recipients," bioRxiv 2023, doi 10.1101/2023.06.16.543190 (author list retrieved from api.biorxiv.org; no journal version located). 97 lung transplant recipients; donor-derived NK detected in recipient blood (n=44); human lung explants contain "CD69+CD103+CD49a+ tissue-resident memory (TRM) T and NK cells." CHICHELNITSKIY AND FALK ARE CO-AUTHORS ON SERGER 2026. The exact human-lung NK origin-tracing methodology — allograft donor/recipient chimerism, a natural congenic transfer — was in-house on the author list and was not applied to the GZMK->ENTPD1 question. This converts "the experiment is hard" into "the experiment was available and not done." It also shows the CD103+CD49a+ residency phenotype pre-exists in non-tumour human lung, so only the ENTPD1+ component of Serger's endpoint is genuinely tumour-restricted.

(4) THE AUTHORS' OWN PREFERRED READING IS SELECTION, stated more strongly in v2 than the auditor quoted. The auditor cited the v1 even-handed "either expands existing... or promotes their induction from CD39- precursors." The v2/published Discussion goes further and picks a side: "our PDTF and in vitro models demonstrate that NKG2A blockade enriches the CD39+ taNK compartment, LIKELY THROUGH EXPANSION OF PRE-EXISTING EFFECTORS and potentially inducing their differentiation from CD39- taNK cells." The canonical alternative — a pre-existing subset is selected/expanded, not converted — is the authors' own leading hypothesis for the only time-resolved experiment in the paper.

NEGATIVE SEARCHES (ran and read; G3): no independent cohort reproducing a GZMK+ -> ENTPD1+ NK ordering was found; no failed-replication paper was found. Recorded as searched-and-not-found, not as non-existent.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
The auditor's G4 coverage was thin — it reached into the CD8 field twice (Mogilenko, Tang) but ran NO search on exhaustion consensus criteria, NO search on TRM parabiosis/transplant-chimerism methodology, NO myeloid search, and NO ILC search. All four home fields were searched here, and all four converge against the claim.

MYELOID — the field that has solved this exact structural problem, and supplies the two controls Serger lacks. Lee CYC, Dean I, Richoz N, ... Withers DR, Clatworthy MR. "In vivo labelling resolves distinct temporal, spatial, and functional properties of tumour macrophages, and identifies subset-specific effects of PD-L1 blockade." Cancer Immunol Res 2025, PMID 40523200 / PMC7617970 (methods read; archived X4adv_myeloid_PMC7617970.txt). Kaede photoconvertible mice give an EXPERIMENTAL TIME-STAMP separating newly-entering from long-resident tumour myeloid cells. Methods verbatim: "the differentiation trajectory was rooted in the Kaede-green dominant cluster, mdTAM_1/monocytes, which represents the cellular subset most associated with newly-infiltrating cells" and — decisively — "No end-points were specified, so the number of trajectories and direction of trajectories were computed without prior bias." That is precisely what Serger did not do: Serger's root was analyst-placed inside NK3_GZMK in BOTH Monocle3 and destiny, and the analysis was steered to a pre-named endpoint ("to gain deeper insight into the transition from NK3_GZMK to NK3_ENTPD1"). The home field's standard is that the root must be certified by an independent time-stamp and the direction left free; when that standard is met, the answer is not a single lineage but two independently-seeded ontogenies (resident-like rTAM vs monocyte-derived mdTAM) with the mdTAM pool "continuously and rapidly replenished by circulating precursors." Consistent with Loyher 2018 (PMID 30201786; parabiosis + fate maps: both origins contribute, proportions shift by site).

TRM / RECRUITMENT-VERSUS-RESIDENCY — the field owns parabiosis, intravascular labelling and transplant chimerism. Applied to human NK (Niehrs 2025, PMID 41087727, detailed above) the answer is transient residency, Runx3-dependent acquisition of residency traits by NEWLY RECRUITED cells, and lymphatic EGRESS. Applied to human lung NK by Serger's own co-authors (Falk group, doi 10.1101/2023.06.16.543190) it yields donor/recipient NK chimerism. The methodology to test X4 in human lung exists, is published, and sits on the author list. Its absence is neglect, not impossibility.

CD8 T CELL / EXHAUSTION — the field has formal consensus criteria and an explicit critique of the term's export. Blank CU, Haining WN, Held W, ... Wherry EJ, Youngblood B, Zehn D. "Defining 'T cell exhaustion'." Nat Rev Immunol 2019, PMID 31570879 / PMC7286441: an 18-expert consensus that anchors exhaustion on a demonstrated precursor-product hierarchy (self-renewing TCF1+ -> terminal TCF1-) and TOX-enforced epigenetic programming — and which concedes that even in CD8 "the developmental relationships are unclear at present." Judge SJ, Murphy WJ, Canter RJ. "Characterizing the Dysfunctional NK Cell: Assessing the Clinical Relevance of Exhaustion, Anergy, and Senescence." Front Cell Infect Microbiol 2020, PMID 32117816 / PMC7031155: "in contrast to the more well-defined and established molecular, genetic, and immunophenotypic characteristics of T cell exhaustion, a consensus on the defining functional and phenotypic features of NK 'exhaustion' is less clear," and exhaustion/anergy/senescence are not separated in NK. Serger labels NK3_ENTPD1 a "dysfunction" state and reads NR4A/exhaustion-associated regulons onto it, importing CD8 vocabulary while satisfying none of the CD8 field's criteria — no antigen receptor, hence no "chronic antigen stimulation"; no demonstrated progenitor-terminal hierarchy; no separation from activation or senescence. This is the same defect the screen's X5 row documents, and X4 inherits it.
 Also from the CD8 field, directly on trajectory epistemics: Schleicher JT, Gupta R, Cerletti D, Sandu I, Oxenius A, Claassen M. "Exploratory trajectory inference reveals CONVERGENT LINEAGES for CD8 T cells in chronic LCMV infection." PLoS One 2025, PMID 40971956 / PMC12448961 — on identical data, trajectory topology and direction are not unique, and convergent (multi-origin) solutions fit as well as divergent ones. Serger reports a single rooted topology with no alternative-root or root-free sensitivity analysis.

ILC — the field named these exact confounds. Kabil A, Shin SB, Hughes MR, McNagny KM. "'Just one word, plastic!': Controversies and caveats in innate lymphoid cell plasticity." Front Immunol 2022, PMID 36052086 / PMC9427196. Verbatim: "this concept of ILC-plasticity is controversial due to several confounding caveats that include, among others, the independent large-scale recruitment of new ILC subsets from distal sites and the local, in situ, differentiation of uncommitted resident precursors." Both confounds are live and uncontrolled in Serger: recruitment is uncontrolled (single timepoint, no chimerism, and NK1/NK2/ILC1 were EXCLUDED before trajectory inference so no alternative progenitor could be recovered by construction), and local differentiation from uncommitted precursors is indistinguishable from conversion of a committed GZMK+ cell.

METHOD'S OWN HOME FIELD (the auditor searched this four times, got 0-1 hits, and recorded the snRNA-velocity caveat as "reasoning, not citation" — here is the citation). Zheng SC, Stein-O'Brien G, Boukas L, Goff LA, Hansen KD. "Pumping the brakes on RNA velocity by understanding and interpreting RNA velocity estimates." Genome Biol 2023, PMID 37885016 / PMC10601342: velocity direction depends critically on k-NN smoothing, producing "considerable estimation errors for both direction and speed... when the k-NN graph fails to accurately represent the true data structure; this is an unknown feature of real data," and they publish a quality measure "that can identify when RNA velocity should not be used." Serger reports no such diagnostic. Bergen V, Soldatov RA, Kharchenko PV, Theis FJ. "RNA velocity - current challenges and future perspectives." Mol Syst Biol 2021, PMID 34435732 / PMC8388041: systematic review of pitfalls and violated assumptions. MultiVelo's streamlines supplied the directional PRIOR that fixed the root for both pseudotime methods, so this is not a peripheral caveat — it is the load-bearing step.

NET G4 VERDICT: every field that can time-stamp cells says the same thing — a cross-sectional expression gradient in a tumour is generated by continuous recruitment, local imprinting and egress acting on populations of mixed origin, and distinguishing that from conversion REQUIRES an experimental timestamp (Kaede, parabiosis, chimerism, barcode). Serger has none, roots the ordering by hand, and analyses only the compartment in which the answer was presupposed.

adv.load_bearing_reason:
MEDIUM is the right grade, but TWO OF THE AUDITOR'S THREE NAMED DEPENDENCIES DO NOT SURVIVE SCRUTINY, and the grade only holds because the third one does.

REJECTED dependency (2), the NKG2A/monalizumab/NCT05221840 rationale. The citation is real — I verified the sentence in v2 — but the trial's rationale rests on the NKG2A-HLA-E axis and on CD39+ taNK being the dominant cytotoxic population, both cross-sectional/functional findings. Nothing in the trial's logic requires that CD39+ cells DESCEND FROM GZMK+ cells. The auditor's own framing gives the game away: it says the therapeutic prediction changes if CD39+ cells are "selected rather than induced" — but that is a claim about the CD39-/CD39+ relationship measured in the PDTF, not about the GZMK->ENTPD1 arrow, and the authors explicitly favour selection there anyway.

REJECTED dependency (1), the in vitro taNK manufacturing platform. It starts from negatively-isolated healthy-donor PERIPHERAL BLOOD NK, not intratumoural GZMK+ NK3, and induces CD103/CD49a/CD39 with IL-15+TGF-beta+irradiated A549 over 6 days. It stands or falls on its own bulk-frequency evidence regardless of whether any intratumoural GZMK+ cell ever becomes ENTPD1+. It is evidence OFFERED FOR the claim, not a downstream consumer OF it; the auditor has the dependency arrow backwards.

UPHELD dependency (3), and it is concrete, named and verifiable in this repository. /home/user/aaa/phaseA/X5.json states in its own downstream_dependency field that X5 "supplies the interpretive frame for X4's ENTPD1+ 'effector/exhausted' end state," and /home/user/aaa/phaseA/X1.json records exhaustion-consensus literature as bearing on "rows X2/X4." X4 is the ONLY recent, named, primary instance in this screen backing X1 ("Organ-resident trNK -> functional intratumoural NK," initial call NEVER TRACED, user-designated highest priority) and X2 ("Newly infiltrating NK -> dysfunctional tumour NK," initial call ESSENTIALLY NO EVIDENCE). Both presuppose that intratumoural NK states are connected by local differentiation; X4 is the concrete citation that presupposition leans on. X4 is additionally ceilinged by D3 ("Human CD56bright NK -> CD56dim NK," MOSTLY INFERENCE), since GZMK marks CD56bright (Bratke 2005, PMID 16106370) and CD39/GZMB the CD56dim-like pole — X4 cannot be graded stronger than D3. My Rebuffet finding TIGHTENS this coupling: if GZMK+ = NK2 = ILCP-derived while the ENTPD1+ endpoint sits in ENKP-derived NK3, then X4 is not merely a weak instance of D3's CD56bright->CD56dim axis but potentially a cross-ONTOGENY claim, which would make X1 and X2 lean on something worse than inference.

ONE DEPENDENCY THE AUDITOR DID NOT NAME, and the most consequential in practice: the arrow is now stated as established fact in the PUBLISHED Sci Immunol abstract — "Trajectory and regulon analyses revealed an inflammation-driven transition from early granzyme K (GZMK)+ NK cells toward an ENTPD1+ (CD39+) effector state characterized by interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) programs." That abstract sentence, not the methods, is the citable unit that will propagate into reviews and grant background sections, and it is precisely the G1 failure mode this screen exists to catch: an abstract asserting "A becomes B" over methods containing only an analyst-rooted pseudotime.

NOT HIGH: the paper's headline conclusions (CD39 marks the dominant cytotoxic taNK population; the state is tumour-restricted, being absent from 50 non-tumour lung donors and from blood; NKG2A blockade potentiates it) are cross-sectional and functional, and all survive intact if the transition is false. NOT LOW: three rows of this screen (X1, X2, X5) route through it, and it now carries a published-abstract assertion.
